# From Chaos to Resilience — Supporting Systems in Production

> Markdown (GEO/AEO) version of <https://mauricio.issei.com.br/en/sustentacao>. Author: **Maurício Yokoyama Issei** · en-BR · Published: 2026-02-20 · Updated: 2026-06-21.

## In short

Supporting critical systems is more than putting out fires: it is a discipline of **reliability, communication and decision under pressure**. The journey goes from reactive chaos to resilience, where incidents have become learning and the system becomes stronger with each failure.

- **Incidents as a sign** — each failure reveals a weakness to be corrected at the root.
- **Measurable reliability** — SLIs/SLOs in place of "stable appearance".
- **Crisis communication** — clarity and cadence reduce collateral damage.
- **Decision under pressure** — previously defined criteria avoid panic in the incident.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is support of production systems?**

It is the discipline to keep critical systems reliable in operation: prevent, detect and respond to incidents, measure reliability (SLIs/SLOs) and learn from each failure to strengthen the system. It goes beyond reactive support — it is reliability engineering.

**How to get out of reactive chaos?**

Changing individual heroism by method: instrument reliability with metrics, define decision criteria before the incident, standardize crisis communication and treat each incident as a learning that corrects the root cause.

**Why does communication matter so much in an incident?**

Because much of the damage to an incident is collateral — customers, teams, and leadership in the dark. Clear communication with defined cadence contains anxiety, aligns the answer and preserves confidence while the problem is solved.
